feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: Dennis Hastert, longtime Republican House speaker who went to prison, dies at age 84
entry.summary: ennis Hastert, whose political legacy as Congress' longest-serving Republican House speaker was later fouled by allegations that he had molested high school athletes during his prior career as a teacher and wrestling coach, has died, a coroner said Monday. He was 84.

entry.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China
entry.summary: The FBI and U.S. prosecutors say Wanying Zhang, also know as Heather, surveilled the Taiwanese president's son and his family.

entry.title: Super El Niño is here. What's so super about it?
entry.summary: This year, federal forecasters say the planet could see the strongest El Niño event on record. Here's what you need to know.

entry.title: Supreme Court's new term kicks off with blockbuster climate change case
entry.summary: The case centers on whether local governments can hold giant energy companies accountable for the local harms of climate change, but it has repercussions beyond climate.

entry.title: People are asking ChatGPT to help them decide how to vote in the midterms
entry.summary: Voters are already voting in the midterms. This year, some voters are trying something new to get ready for the election: asking AI to help research their ballot and even decide who to vote for.

entry.title: Sexual assault survivors share stories online following Cornell rape allegations
entry.summary: Hearing about the sexual assault of a Cornell University student in 2024 is bringing back memories for people who have experienced abuse. With the story everywhere, it's hard to ignore.

entry.title: The USDA's largest and oldest lab is set to close
entry.summary: The USDA's flagship agricultural research lab could close this week. Scientists warn that could hurt U.S. food supply.

entry.title: In 'Ply,' Hernán Díaz imagines what we become after the world we know
entry.summary: Pulitzer prize winner Hernán Díaz' new book 'Ply' follows a young woman who siphons electricity to power punk shows in a re-wilded world. Díaz tells NPR how the novel came to examine selfhood, identity and intimacy.

entry.title: Supreme Court starts a new term with a case about who pays for climate damage
entry.summary: The Supreme Court starts its new term with a Colorado county's claim that an oil refinery worsened climate change. The ruling could determine whether similar cases can move forward.

entry.title: How much are AI data centers adding to your electricity bill?
entry.summary: Americans are worried AI data centers will raise their electricity bills. Congress has come up with a plan to protect ratepayers, but there's no easy way to find out what AI is costing them.
